findings.section: 2.2.4 Open Permission Latch (Reconcile-Required, Sticky Until Cleared) — CP-001
findings.description: The fallback for `position_reconcile_epsilon` is stated as a parenthetical default, not a required runtime behavior. A looser implementation fallback could hide position drift and clear the latch early.

evidence.quote: - Exchange positions match ledger cumulative fills within `position_reconcile_epsilon` (default: instrument's `min_amount` or `1e-6` if undefined).

findings.proposed_fix: Require runtime to MUST use `min_amount`, or `1e-6` when undefined, as the reconciliation fallback epsilon.

findings.section: 2.2.4 Open Permission Latch (Reconcile-Required, Sticky Until Cleared) — CP-001
findings.description: The trade-lookback criterion does not specify fail-closed handling for nonpositive or otherwise invalid `reconcile_trade_lookback_sec`. A bad lookback can miss recent trades and unblock OPEN prematurely.

evidence.quote: No missing trades over the last `reconcile_trade_lookback_sec` (default: 300s) as determined by REST `/get_user_trades` query.

findings.proposed_fix: Specify that unset, nonpositive, or invalid lookback values MUST default to 300s or cause reconciliation to fail closed.

findings.section: 2.2.4 Open Permission Latch (Reconcile-Required, Sticky Until Cleared) — CP-001
findings.description: The startup fallback and warning for invalid `reconcile_stall_max_delay_s` is normative, but this section has no acceptance test that proves the 30s default and startup warning behavior.

evidence.quote: - If `reconcile_stall_max_delay_s` is missing or ≤ 0 at startup, runtime MUST treat it as the default (30s) and emit a startup warning log.

findings.proposed_fix: Add an AT covering missing or ≤0 `reconcile_stall_max_delay_s` and verifying 30s fallback plus startup warning emission.
